subject: toucan
reasoning:
I need to build a toucan model using the SDK, keeping it to a single reasonably-sized TypeScript module. I'm planning out the structure using the builder API's joints, chains, and sweep methods to construct the body parts efficiently.

Other functions I should use include rod, capsule, lathe, extrude, and surface for shaping geometry, plus paint functions like gradient and countershade for coloring. For the toucan itself, I'll give it a large orange-yellow beak with a black tip, a mostly black body, and a white throat and chest bib for the classic toucan look.

I'm now sketching out the actual proportions and coordinates: a perched bird standing with feet at ground level, legs bent at the tarsus, a torso tilted from pelvis to chest, a neck rising to the head, and a beak built as upper and lower mandibles swept forward from the head, roughly matching real toco toucan proportions scaled into meters.

Writing beak sweep geometry...

For the body I'm planning a mottled dark black texture with a white throat bib placed via sector bands around the chest, and a black tail rendered as an angled box sweep tapering toward the rear.

I'm figuring out how to add toucan-specific details: a red undertail sector, a blue eye-ring built from a small sphere stuck to the nearest surface point near the head, and modeling the head and body as a lofted shape running along station points from tail to neck.

Now I'm sketching out the skeleton structure, starting with a root pelvis joint and a spine chain running from pelvis through chest to neck base, working through how the chain function assigns parent joints and names to each segment along a smooth catmull path.

Actually, I'll go with explicit joints for everything rather than chains, since sweeps can take a bone as a list of joints laid onto a path — that keeps naming deterministic and consistent for the body loft spanning hips through chest, neck, and head.

I'm laying out the joint hierarchy: hips as root, then chest, neck, and head each parented to the previous, with positions moving upward and forward along the body, plus starting on the beak joints next.

Now I'm sketching the beak joints (upper beak rigid, lower jaw with a hinge role) and then the leg joints — hip, knee, ankle, and toes on each side — working out approximate positions for a short bird leg tucked into the body.

For the toes I'm going zygodactyl-style: three forward-fanned and one back, built as rod sweeps running from ankle through toe tips, using the joint frames themselves as path points since those accept frame inputs directly.

Now I'm thinking through the wings — folded bird wings using either a sweep with a tapering chord radius from shoulder to tip, or an extrude of a wing outline lying flat in the XZ plane, leaning toward the extrude approach for a cleaner flat-wing silhouette.

I'm attaching wings to the chest bone, placing them symmetrically at x=±0.075 since the YZ-plane outline mirrors itself naturally across X. For the tail, I'm sweeping a tapering box section along a catmull-rom spline from the hips, tracking width and height per joint.

Now I'm defining the main body as a loft bound to the hips-chest-neck-head bone chain, with stations sized to give a compact toucan silhouette — wider through the mid-body and chest, narrowing toward the tail base and neck — then adding a separate head loft with its own stations for the rounded skull shape.

For the bill, I'm placing it as a sweep from the face base out to a tapered tip, with radius functions shrinking the width and height along the length to get that characteristic toucan shape, and assigning orange coloring with a black band near the tip.

The lower jaw gets its own joint and sweep, parented to the head, with a smaller taper so the mandible sits naturally closed against the upper bill. For the eyes, I'm figuring out placement using the head's surface mesh to find the nearest point near the expected eye location so I can attach a small eye patch accurately rather than guessing coordinates blindly.

Now I'm placing stuck geometry for the eyes: a small blue torus ring around the socket and a black sphere pupil on top, using surface normals from the head sweep to orient and embed them correctly. I'm also planning the white bib on the chest using a sector range over the body loft, and treating the facial skin area as bare dark coloring consistent with toucan anatomy.

For the body color, I'm layering a mottled paint texture over the black feathers for subtle variation, and applying a red sector to the undertail region while keeping the rest of the tail black. I'm making sure these sector fills are treated as paints too, so the coloring stays consistent with the overall painting system rather than flat colors.

Now I'm sketching out the skeleton joint hierarchy with approximate positions: hips as the root, chest and neck branching upward, head with jaw and bill attachments, and legs branching down through hip, knee, and ankle joints on each side, all parented appropriately so the rig deforms naturally.

For the feet, I'm placing toe rods extending from each ankle toward the ground at slight forward and outward angles, checking that the lowest points sit close to y=0 within tolerance. For the tail, I'm defining a path from the hips through two intermediate tail joints out to a tail tip, planning to sweep this path with matching bone weights so the tail follows the skeleton smoothly.

Now I'm setting up the wing geometry as an extrusion from the chest bone, working out the local coordinate frame so the thickness axis aligns along X, and positioning the wing's span in z relative to the shoulder joint.

I'm then checking the wing fits against the body's half-width at the attachment point, confirming it sits flush against the torso surface with a slight lift. From there I'm defining the body loft stations (width/height pairs at various heights from rear to neck) and sketching out a separate head loft that picks up where the neck station leaves off, though the two overlap slightly and need reconciling.

I'm merging everything into one continuous loft from tail to head using a bone list spanning hips, chest, neck, and head, running a catmull-rom sweep through roughly seven stations. For coloring, I'm planning the head as black with a white bib across the throat and chest, estimating the sector range along the t parameter (around 0.5 to 0.85) to approximate where the toucan's distinctive white chest patch should sit relative to the loft's arc-length.

Now I'm positioning the bill as a separate sweep anchored inside the head rather than floating outside it — the upper bill curves from the head front near z 0.16 out to a tip around z 0.38, with the width and height tapering from base to tip, while the lower bill sits slightly below and tapers similarly for a naturally shaped jaw. I'm also working out the color assignment for the bill itself.

Rather than a flat fill, I decide to use a custom paint function on the bill geometry that checks the z-position of each point: orange near the base, transitioning to yellow mid-bill, then black near the tip, mimicking a toucan's characteristic multi-colored beak, applying the same scheme to the lower bill.

I'm picking colors for the other features too — grey-blue feet, a blue eye ring with a dark pupil, mottled black body plumage, and a red undertail patch — while deciding to skip finer cosmetic details like nostril carving or wing patches to limit complexity.

For the eyes, I plan to attach torus-ring and sphere geometries to the head surface using nearest-point hits, rotating the torus geometry so its flat face aligns with the surface normal, and placing mirrored pairs on both sides of the head.

For the legs and feet, I'm using rod and sweep functions bound to joint chains with explicit colors, since the color is mandatory unless gradient bands are defined, and I verify how bone-weighting works across a loft that spans from tail to head through hips, chest, neck, and head joints.

I'm also mapping out the body's tilt and proportions — the tail arcing down and back with a tapering box cross-section, the body sloping diagonally upward from tail to head at roughly a 30-40 degree angle to mimic a perched posture, and checking that the legs and feet meet the ground plane correctly beneath the body.

Now I'm scaffolding the actual builder code: setting up imports, defining color constants including a mottled feather texture and the paint function for the bill, then creating the joint hierarchy starting from hips up through chest, neck, head, and the bill/jaw joints, followed by hip and leg joints — weighing whether to use plain joints or chain structures for the legs to properly support bone weighting.

Still writing joint hierarchy...

I'm reasoning through how the chain function resolves parent bones by checking weights on the path input, falling back to finding the nearest existing joint, and deciding to just pass hips explicitly as the parent for clarity; then I work out how chain spans and names map onto knot positions along a polyline so the knee joint lands exactly at the middle path point.

I continue defining the leg sweep geometry with a smooth-fillet corner at the knee, then add capsule-shaped toes extending from the ankle joint at specific offsets, making sure their radius and vertical placement bring them flush with the ground, and set up a side-mirrored helper so left and right legs share the same logic with negated x-coordinates.

Now I'm laying out the body's loft stations — a sequence of position, width, and height values from the tail to the face — tuning each station's dimensions to shape the neck, head, and bill transition, and setting up loft options including bone bindings, side count, and a white sector for a belly/bib patch.

Writing tail sweep code...

I'm defining the upper and lower bill as separate sweeps with tapering box-ish cross sections, binding each to its own joint (upperBill and jaw) and applying the custom bill paint, then setting up the eye geometry — a rotated torus ring plus a small dark sphere — stuck onto the nearest surface point on each side of the head using the surface/hit system.

I'm now designing the wings as extruded outline shapes defined by a set of 2D points representing a folded wing silhouette, positioning them relative to the shoulder with a tapering thickness and binding them to the chest joint, then mirroring the same outline for the opposite side; I note that more detailed wing coverts or accent patterns could be added but decide to skip them for simplicity, and move toward finalizing the return value and export of the builder function along with its metadata.

I go through a final type-check pass across all the pieces — joint options, chain/path typings, sector tuples for sweeps, paint function signatures, and bone bindings — and confirm proportions by checking how legs, wings, and tail connect to the body stations so nothing overlaps awkwardly. I settle on coloring the head black with a white bib and the bill using z-based color thresholds for black, yellow, and orange bands, then prepare to write out the complete, cleaned-up final code with the default exported builder function returning the baked root model.
